public_rationale: There is material evidence against a broad claim of construction incapacity: Crusoe energized initial Abilene buildings, and Core Scientific reported substantial billable capacity. But those records do not establish completion and sufficiency of the expansion discussed. Crusoe’s June 2026 update still distinguished two operating buildings from six under construction. With no stated deadline and no conclusive delivery or failure event, the forecast remains unresolved.
limitations: A narrower reading that neither company could deliver any relevant capacity would fare worse against the evidence.
Company disclosures establish reported milestones, not independently verified full-project acceptance.
Later construction targets are not deadlines supplied by Zitron.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning Construction of the multi-building campus
evidence.explanation: The disclosure places energization within a year of the June 2024 construction start and reports early training and inference workloads by publication. This is material evidence of delivery capability, but covers the initial phase.

The same paragraph specifically reports two operational buildings and six still under construction at the planned 1.2 GW Abilene campus. Contracted portfolio capacity therefore cannot establish completion of that campus.

The reported billable capacity demonstrates operating delivery at company level. The release does not establish that this entire capacity serves OpenAI or completes the expansion described in the claim; the accompanying revenue figure is not used.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Project-specific commissioning and customer-acceptance records establishing delivery of the relevant expansion, or definitive records of abandonment caused by inability to deliver.
